findings: A maximum-minimum thermometer had gone up by the gate overnight. -> A maximum-minimum thermometer had been put up by the gate overnight. (passage, para 2, sentence 4 - new in fleet-repair-1)

justification: Native read-aloud of all five layers, with two sentences read either side of every repaired span. Round-1 vote-1 findings are both discharged: “about four hundred livery yards” now settles the stable-yard sense at first mention, and Pallenmoor’s middle quoted sentence is now real speech - “I can’t put a number on it; these readings won’t carry one, and the blend on the grains changes from one supplier to the next” reads aloud as talk, with “one” doing clean anaphora on “a number”. The rebuilt instrument paragraph is otherwise sound: “a steel cone on a rod, under a ring weight raised to a collar and let fall” is compressed but parses on one pass, “It gives two figures - how deep the cone sinks on the first blow, and how many blows take it to a hundred millimetres” is plain, and the elided comparands in “two-thirds as deep” and “nearly doubled” are parallel and licensed by the colon. “Though not in the way the yard had blamed it” now has “it” bound to “the machine” in the same sentence and reads naturally, so the round-1 vote-2 pronoun complaint is discharged at the read-aloud level too. The new mid-scene close lands well: the callback from the gate thermometer to “the thermometer beside them reads four” is the best sentence the repair added. Two stumbles remain, both in new text. “The thermometer had gone up” is the standard way of saying the reading rose, and “by the gate overnight” only retracts that a beat later, so a reader briefly gets a temperature rise in a paragraph whose whole point is that the morning was cold. And “a winter month of lessons” inverts the natural modifier order; the money is being compared to a month of winter lessons, not to a winter-flavoured month. No comma splice, no verbless fragment outside deliberate use, and no composed-prose sentence inside speech marks. Flag, not kill.

are ones he “would trust from hardly any of them” -> He has readings from a hundred and forty arenas, and the injury records that might have joined the two are ones he “would trust from hardly any of them” (q4 rationale, option B rebuttal)

justification: Systematic class-by-class sweep. Misquotation, tested mechanically: every curly-quoted span in all five rationales, all prompts and all options was extracted and tested for membership in the passage after normalising quotes, dashes and whitespace - 30 of 30 verbatim, 0 near-misses, including all seven spans that are new or newly re-anchored by the repair (“changes from one supplier to the next”, “raised to a collar and let fall”, “how many blows take it to a hundred millimetres”, “in the cold the first blow took the cone two-thirds as deep, and the count nearly doubled”, “The gap between my February morning and my July afternoon…”, “is careful, and the care is the most useful thing about him”, “The tester measures a surface; there is no horse above the cone”). Round-1 vote-2 findings are both discharged: the quoted blend is now “the blend on the grains”, which is consistent with grains “coated in wax” and no longer contradicts the build, and “the yard had blamed it” supplies the antecedent the old “the yard meant it” lacked. Countability, tense/aspect (has been back, had gone up, had not been turned, have been dropped + a closed-period past simple), NPIs, relatives, zero relatives with gaps, register: clean. Four residuals, three of them introduced by the repair. Worst is a direction inversion in the q4 key rationale: the passage’s “That is a good deal less than the trade’s brochures offer” refers to the modest claim Pallenmoor does make, so “what he will not claim” makes the refused, larger claim the smaller of the two - and the same rationale’s D paragraph gets it right with “what he says”, which is the internal proof of the error. Second, the q4 B rebuttal lifts “from hardly any of them” into a frame where “them” has no antecedent at all; the hundred and forty arenas are in the passage, not in the rationale. Third, the q1 key rationale says the two figures “moved the same way” when they move in opposite arithmetic directions, which is exactly what the key option states (“a shallower first blow and a higher count”), so the summary line teaches against its own key. Fourth, “The heaters” takes a definite article on first mention with no antecedent and only a weak bridge from temperature; heaters are never raised as an option before this sentence. (“The pan” two clauses earlier is a genuine trade definite bridging to the layer already described as “firm enough to lean a spade on”, and is left alone.)

justification: Native read-aloud of all five layers, reading two sentences either side of every repaired span. The new passage token “realise it” reads as ordinary situational “it” (realise the mistake) and does not need an overt nominal antecedent. The rebuilt options sit naturally in their frames when read aloud with the key in place: “Although what a hall gives an eight-year-old is wholehearted, it is not permitted to run long” and “will give one dutifully” both scan. “Four or five seconds, then a ragged tail…, then the scrape of a chair” is a deliberate verbless fragment in an essayistic register, not a defect. One stumble, in a sentence adjacent to the rewritten gap-3 preposition material: “the far end of the process from the one being described” makes the reader hunt for what “the one” picks out (an end? a process? a stage?), and it is the only place in the unit where a first pass fails. Worth naming for the record without a finding: this unit carries the copular-epigram tic hardest of the four - six authorial epigrams in 372 words (“That is the part worth noticing”, “first is the exposed position”, “That is why the second pair of hands matters more…”, “Ending is the harder half”, “The tail is the seam”, “the refusal is the message”), plus two cloze frames that are themselves copular. Cloze integrity after the option swaps: gap 1 four sentence-initial adverbs, gap 2 four bare verbs each forming a real phrasal with in, gap 3 four singular abstract nouns of one stock, gap 4 four adjectives (rehearsed and outspoken participial, brief and wholehearted plain - still one word class), gap 5 four -ly manner adverbs. Every gap is POS-uniform and in every gap exactly one option is idiomatic in context; the two new distractors are wrong on the right grounds - “brief” fails the concession because it agrees with the clause “Although” is meant to pull it against, and “eagerly” fails because the sentence denies that this room’s sound is the warm one. One residual, in new text: “clapping from keenness” takes the wrong causal preposition - English pairs an emotion or motive noun with “out of” (out of politeness, out of duty, out of keenness), and “from” in a rationale whose job is teaching collocation is the wrong place for it. Native read-aloud of all five layers, reading two sentences either side of every repaired span. Every change fleet-repair-1 made to this unit improves the read. “Carriers drop out of the wall into a bin, one a minute” drops round 1’s “padded”, which had been pre-empting the remedy in the opening line, and the new closing beat “Another carrier hits the foam.” now pays that setup off - the definite “the foam” bridges cleanly to “Two bins are lined with foam”, and the scene closes on the mechanism instead of stating it. “Between stations the shocks were tiny” is a better instrument report than “the trace barely moved” and is plainer aloud. Ashvenor’s speech is untouched and still the hardest thing in the format done right - a deictic opener, a contracted causal chain, a first-person hedge, and a genuine spoken cleft (“It’s the stop at the far end that does it”). No comma splice, no garden path, no composed-prose sentence inside speech marks, no verbless fragment. One thing the repair thinned rather than broke: round 1’s explicit “What changed is the bins” is gone, so the bins-were-changed reading now rests on the contrast with “The loop runs at the speed it always has” and on the “and” in “Two bins are lined with foam, and rejects are down by about half”. A native reader takes that without effort and it is the correct reading, so no finding - but it is the one inference in the batch that got softer rather than firmer. Incidentally the same deletion removed this unit’s only copular epigram: the tic is now at zero here, the lowest of the four.

Systematic class-by-class sweep. Misquotation, tested mechanically: all 7 curly-quoted spans in the single rationale extracted and tested for membership in the passage - 7 of 7 verbatim, and critically the one span the repair put at risk, “the shocks were tiny”, now matches the rewritten passage sentence exactly (round 1’s passage read “the trace barely moved”, so a rationale left unrepaired here would have produced the batch’s only misquotation; it did not). No stale quote survives anywhere: the deleted “What changed is the bins” is not quoted in the rationale, which paraphrases it as “The change was to the bins, two of which are now lined with foam”. Mechanism direction, the class most likely to fail in this unit, is still right in both halves and still explicitly closed by the rationale’s final paragraph: potassium is intracellular, the cells burst in transit, the potassium therefore passes out into the plasma, the reported figure comes out too high and not too low, and the pink is haemoglobin released from the cells rather than something present beforehand. The remedy direction is also right - the loop speed was left alone, the landing bins changed, and the fall in rejects follows the change and not a slowdown, which is exactly what option A gets wrong. Prepositions are BrE-idiomatic and uncalqued (round the loop, taped into a carrier, holds a spun tube to the window, down by about half, hits the foam). Countability (blood gases as clinical plural, rejects as plural count, shocks as count), articles (the new indefinite “a bin” correctly precedes the definite “the foam”), tense/aspect, NPIs (Nothing shows, never gone - licensed), relatives, zero relatives with gaps, pronoun reach (they/their bound to “the cells”; “sent it round the loop” to the carrier), mixed comparisons (“higher than the patient’s” is number against number by possessive ellipsis) and register: all clean. Nothing to report.

Variety and typography per layer, plus the batch-level quote-terminal ruling. Declared BrE and held in the student-facing layers, not only the rationale: title (“Blood by Tube”) - none; passage - colour, haemoglobin, plus BrE lexis “senior biomedical scientist”, “round the loop”, “porter”, “the ward”; prompt - none; options - colour, spoilt, ward; rationale - colour, haemoglobin, porter, ward. Targeted AmE regex over all five layers (color/hemoglobin/spoiled/analyzed/-ize/-ization/center/fiber/meter/percent/railroad/neighbor and the rest) returned zero hits; the only “fall” token is the noun in “a fall in rejects”, variety-neutral. Typography per layer, counted: title all zero; passage U+2019=4 U+0027=0 U+2013=1 (byline) U+2014=0; prompt all zero; options all zero; rationale U+2019=2 U+0027=0 U+2013=0 U+2014=0. No straight quote of either kind, no em dash, the single hyphen word-internal (likely-sounding), zero space-hyphen-space. The repair added no typographic character of any new class. The ruling, made at batch level and reversing round-1 vote 3: this unit is correct and must not be changed. It applies the codified BrE source-governed rule in all five of its terminal cases without a single miss - the stop goes inside for the three colon-introduced spans that quote a complete sentence the passage itself terminates with a full stop (“The loop runs at the speed it always has.”, “Nothing shows on the ward; the colour comes with the spinning.”, “Blood gases have never gone by tube; a porter walks those down.”), and outside for the two where the source does not terminate there (“It’s the stop at the far end that does it”, which the passage ends with a comma before the speech tag, and the mid-sentence fragment “rejects are down by about half”). That is not internal inconsistency; it is the rule working. The divergence is real but it sits in 001 (two colon-introduced cases) and 004 (one), which place the stop outside in the identical construction; 002 is not a party, having no complete-sentence terminal quotes at all. Normalising those three toward this unit costs nothing in quote fidelity, because the passage does terminate those sentences with a full stop at exactly the quoted point - whereas normalising this unit outward, as round 1 prescribed, would strip terminal punctuation the source actually has. Clean.

Native read-aloud of all five layers, reading two sentences either side of every repaired span. The round-1 vote-1 finding is discharged outright: “The letters run to March, over a gate and some stones” is gone, taking the run-over garden path with it, and the replacement “The letters run to March; both sides agree the thorn was last laid in 1839” is clean on one pass - the semicolon joins two clauses that genuinely belong together, since the agreement is something the letters record. The new third sentence, “An ash grew in the stone gap; a culvert ran under the lane”, reads as ordinary terse boundary description; “grew” is stative-descriptive here, not inchoative, which is what this annalistic register wants. The re-pegged “from the ash to the culvert” is unforced and does not announce the inference it enables. The definites in the new sentence (“the stone gap”, “the lane”) are scene-setting definites of the kind a period boundary record uses as a matter of course, and the rebuilt options carry no stumble (“put the railway plan into the letters”, “left untended”, “after the attorneys had begun to write” all read native). Period register still right and unforced - thorn bank, cut from above and cleaned from below, laid, the enclosure, deposited plan, chained and pegged, no land was taken - and “attorney” remains period-correct for 1845 rather than an Americanism. Past perfects sequence correctly against the 1845 anchor and the archival present (“The letters run”, “both sides agree”) is consistent with itself. No comma splice, no verbless fragment, no quoted speech to go wrong, and the copular-epigram tic is at zero. Nothing to report.

The endpoint inference the key rests on is airtight in English: the ash is in the stone gap, the culvert is under the lane, so the two pairs of landmarks denote the same two places, and nothing in the passage lets a reader tie them any other way. Chronology still checks (October 1845 pegging, November 1845 claim, letters to March, February offer, scheme abandoned autumn 1846, thorn laid again 1851; 1839 is six years before the first letter and an unremarkable point in a laying cycle that the 1839-to-1851 interval itself corroborates). Countability (timber as mass), articles (“the line” bridges to the deposited plan in the sentence before), tense/aspect, NPIs (never, no land, never fell due - all licensed), relatives (who only of persons), zero relatives with gaps, pronoun reach, mixed comparisons and register: clean.
